newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese army comander on frontline with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese army comander on frontline with Israel.

text.p: Lebanese army commander General Emile Lahoud inspected on Tuesday frontline units facing Israeli troops in south Lebanon and ordered them to defend Lebanese territory by all possible means.
An army communique said Lahoud inspected positions of the army's sixth brigade and commando units confronting the Israelis at the south of Lebanon's eastern Bekaa valley.
The troops face Israeli units at the eastern end of a 15-km (nine miles) wide occupied buffer zone intended to prevent cross-border guerrilla raids into Israel.

"He (Lahoud) gave orders to the soldiers emphasising that since Syrian-Israeli (peace) talks stopped the Israeli enemy is trying its utmost to separate the Lebanese and Syrian tracks and is resorting to threats," the communique said.
"The army's duty is to protect its land and counter the enemy with all available means," it added.
Lebanon has reinforced its frontline in the Bekaa valley in the past few days with hundreds of commandos backed by artillery and armoured vehicles.

The reinforcement followed a redeployment of some of Syria's 35,000 soldiers in Lebanon in what was described as a defensive measure after apparent threats of military action in Lebanon by Israeli leaders.
Lahoud told the frontline troops that Israeli threats would make the Lebanese army hold on more strongly to its territory in coordination with Syria.
Lebanese army officials said before the recent reinforcement that nearly half Lebanon's 63,000-strong army was deployed in the south.
They told Reuters that five of the army's 11 mechanised brigades were deployed in the south.

The Lebanese army also has five special forces battalions, a commando battalion and a paratroop battalion, the officials said. It has about 150 old U.S., French and Soviet-built tanks, some 4-500 armoured personnel carriers and 16 second-hand Bell helicopters.
